name: Naples
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Naples: supplier and contractor vetting, public procurement exposure, port counterparties and court support.
hero_lede: Naples is southern Italy's largest urban economy, built on its port, shipbuilding, aerospace, food production and tourism. TDSC scopes investigative consulting from Nashville for matters touching the city, coordinating Italian counsel and appropriately licensed local investigators where work in Italy is required.
intro: Naples is the capital of Campania and the centre of a metropolitan city of 92 comuni with about 2.95 million residents according to ISTAT data for January 2026. It is commonly ranked as one of Italy's largest urban economies, resting on commerce, manufacturing, construction, logistics and a large public sector. The Port of Naples is one of the busiest in the Mediterranean for cargo, ferries and cruise traffic. The wider area hosts shipyards in Naples, Pozzuoli and Castellammare di Stabia, a light aircraft and aerospace supply base, and well-known food industries including Gragnano pasta, tomato processing, dairy and coffee roasting. Tourism to the city, Pompeii, the islands and the Amalfi coast is a major and growing source of income.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Naples mainly because of counterparty and integrity risk. The local economy is dominated by small firms, and court proceedings show that Camorra groups have sought to infiltrate public works and other contracts: in 2023 the Naples anti-mafia directorate secured 18 precautionary measures over tenders in Caivano, and in June 2025 the Naples tribunal convicted eight defendants over a hospital renovation contract at the Cardarelli. Investors, lenders, contractors and buyers therefore want to know who stands behind suppliers, subcontractors, property sellers and acquisition targets, and whether their histories match what they present.

matters.title: Contractor and subcontractor vetting
matters.text: Construction, renovation and services contracts in the Naples area have been targets for criminal infiltration. We research ownership, directors, related companies, litigation and adverse media on contractors and subcontractors, helping clients and counsel decide whether to engage and what safeguards to apply.

matters.title: Public procurement and concession exposure
matters.text: Companies bidding for or partnering on public contracts in Campania need to know whether partners or subcontractors have been named in anti-mafia or corruption proceedings. We review published judgments, press coverage and corporate records to identify links that could jeopardise a tender or concession.

matters.title: Port and logistics counterparties
matters.text: Shippers, insurers and traders working through the Port of Naples rely on forwarders, hauliers, terminal service providers and customs agents. We research their ownership, history and connections, and support inquiries after cargo losses or suspected diversion, working alongside the client's Italian counsel.

matters.title: Acquisitions in food and manufacturing
matters.text: Investors buying into Campanian food, pasta, dairy or industrial businesses need assurance on owners, family holdings, related-party dealings and past disputes. We map corporate structures through the Italian business register and public sources and test management representations before signing.

matters.title: Hospitality and property transactions
matters.text: Hotel, short-let and property investments in Naples, the islands and the Amalfi coast can involve opaque sellers and intermediaries. We research sellers, holding companies and financing sources, and flag litigation, insolvency and adverse media, so that counsel can structure transactions and warranties accordingly.

local_context.title: Naples courts and prosecutors
local_context.text: The Tribunale di Napoli and the Corte d'Appello di Napoli sit in the city, and the Naples tribunal hosts a specialised business section for company and intellectual property matters. The Naples Public Prosecutor's Office includes the district anti-mafia directorate (DDA), which leads Camorra investigations across the district. Published judgments and reporting of criminal trials, such as the 2025 Cardarelli contracts ruling, are useful research sources.

local_context.title: Prefecture and anti-infiltration measures
local_context.text: The Prefecture of Naples plays a central role in preventing criminal infiltration of the economy. In July 2024 the Prefect, the Naples Chief Prosecutor and Confartigianato Imprese Napoli signed a protocol for legality and business security, aimed at preventing infiltration and encouraging businesses to report extortion and usury. Prefectural anti-mafia measures affecting companies are relevant to counterparty assessments and should be checked with counsel.

local_context.title: Business register and Chamber
local_context.text: Companies based in the area are entered in the business register kept by the Naples Chamber of Commerce (CCIAA di Napoli) as part of the national Registro delle Imprese. Official extracts show legal representatives, directors, registered capital, filings and, for many company types, shareholders. Records on small family businesses can be thin, so register data is combined with court records, media and site-level information.

local_context.title: Port authority and maritime cluster
local_context.text: The Port of Naples is administered by a port system authority that also covers other Campanian ports. Port concessions, terminal operators and maritime service providers are a recurring focus of diligence, alongside shipyards in Naples, Pozzuoli and Castellammare di Stabia, where Fincantieri operates a major yard. Concession holders and their subcontractors are usually traceable through public notices and the business register.

tdsc_approach: TDSC has no office in Naples and works on Naples matters from Nashville. We agree the purpose with the client's Italian counsel first, whether vetting a contractor, assessing a tender partner, reviewing a port counterparty or supporting a transaction or dispute, and scope research to that purpose. Sources include the Registro delle Imprese, published judgments, press reporting of Naples criminal and civil proceedings, and records in other jurisdictions where counterparties are based. Italy licenses private investigators, so any fieldwork in Campania is carried out by appropriately licensed Italian professionals, and personal data is handled under the GDPR and Italian rules. We do not approach or confront suspected criminal groups; such matters belong to the authorities.

faqs.q: Can TDSC check whether a Naples supplier has Camorra links?
faqs.a: We research the supplier's ownership, directors, related companies, litigation and adverse media, including published judgments and reporting of anti-mafia proceedings in Naples. Findings indicate risk and its sources; they are not a criminal determination. Formal anti-mafia certifications and prefectural measures are matters for the authorities and Italian counsel, and any fieldwork is done by licensed Italian investigators.

faqs.q: Which courts handle business disputes in Naples?
faqs.a: The Tribunale di Napoli hears civil and commercial cases and has a specialised business section for company and intellectual property disputes. Appeals go to the Corte d'Appello di Napoli. Part of the metropolitan area falls within other court districts, such as Napoli Nord, so the correct venue depends on where a party is based and should be confirmed with counsel.

faqs.q: How reliable are business register records for small Neapolitan firms?
faqs.a: The Registro delle Imprese, kept locally by the Naples Chamber of Commerce, provides official data on directors, capital and filings, and often shareholders. Many local firms are small or family-run, filings can be minimal and nominee arrangements occur. We therefore combine register data with court records, media, property information and, where lawful and needed, local inquiries.

faqs.q: Can you support investors in Naples hospitality and property?
faqs.a: Yes. For hotel, short-let and property deals in Naples, the islands or the Amalfi coast, we research sellers, holding structures, managers and financing sources, and flag litigation, insolvency and adverse media. The results help counsel set warranties and conditions. Title searches and notarial checks remain with the Italian notary handling the transaction.

Yes. Court records, register extracts, prefectural notices and most local reporting on Naples are in Italian, and coverage of criminal proceedings appears in national and Neapolitan media. TDSC works with Italian-language sources and provides English summaries, noting where a translation or legal interpretation should be confirmed by Italian counsel.
